description: List a language's sets, each with its `id`, `name`, `platform`, `releaseDate`, `serie` and card counts — the values a `set` filter takes. Oldest first unless `sort` or `order` say otherwise: `order` 'desc' lists the newest first. `contains` and `platform` filter the whole catalogue before paging.

contains.description: Case-insensitive substring of the id or name, applied before paging.

language.description: Catalogue language. Names, values and set lists are localised (the Asian catalogues have their own set ids), so look values up in it; prices are the same in every language.

order.description: Whether the order runs ascending or descending — 'desc' on `releaseDate` puts the newest set first.

page.description: Zero-indexed page. A page past the end is an empty success with `hasMore` false.

platform.description: 'TCG' for printed sets, 'TCG Pocket' for digital ones; applied before paging. Some catalogues hold only one.

size.description: Results per page; only `hasMore` says whether more exist.

name: list_sets

hasMore.description: True when at least one further page of results exists after this one. Request every result by incrementing 'page' until this is false. There is deliberately no total count: the length of the returned array is the size of this page.

language.description: The catalogue language this response was read in.

order.description: 'asc' (default) or 'desc'; 'desc' by `releaseDate` lists the newest set first.

page.description: The zero-indexed page of results this response holds, whether it was requested or defaulted to.

sets.description: One page of sets, in the requested language, after any 'contains' and 'platform' filters. Catalogues differ enormously in size — 220 sets in English against 2 in Polish — so a set missing here is missing from that language rather than from the game.

cardCount.description: How large the set is, which is what tells a caller how many pages of search_cards results to expect from it.

official.description: How many cards are numbered in the set's printed run, which is the highest 'localId' a caller should expect to see.

total.description: How many cards the set holds in total, including secret rares numbered beyond the official count.

id.description: The set's id, and the value to pass to search_cards' 'set' filter, e.g. 'swsh3' or 'sv04.5'. Not derived from the name in any predictable way, which is why guessing one does not work.

name.description: The set's printed name in the requested language, e.g. 'Darkness Ablaze' or, in French, 'Ténèbres Embrasées'. Also accepted by search_cards' 'set' filter, matched exactly.

platform.description: Whether the set was physically printed as part of the Trading Card Game, or exists only in the digital game Pokémon TCG Pocket. Cards in a Pocket set carry no regulation mark and no tournament legality, because the Trading Card Game's formats do not apply to them.

releaseDate.description: The date the set was released, as 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

serie.description: The series this set belongs to, which is what groups sets into an era.

name.description: The series' printed name, e.g. 'Scarlet & Violet'.

size.description: The page size this response was built with, whether it was requested or defaulted to. It is the maximum number of results this page can hold, not the number it does hold — the last page holds fewer.

sort.description: What the sets were ordered by, whether requested or defaulted to.
